title: Agent Talk service document
description: /.well-known/agent-talk-service.json: who a service is, where its keys are, the carriers it takes direct steps on, and where an address's door document is. An open door's document is the same with door. Signed in signatures.
$comment: Checks only code can do: issuer equal to the domain the document was fetched for; a signature in signatures (the reader may stop after eight) whose protected header is { alg: EdDSA, kid, typ: agent-talk-service } and that verifies, with the payload being the document in JCS (RFC 8785) without signatures, against a key the reader already holds for issuer. A reader ignores a carrier type it does not know and fields this version does not define. The reference implementation holds issuer to at most 128 characters and door.address to at most 500, where this schema asks for an issuer domain and an address.

carriers.description: The carriers the service takes direct steps on. Empty: the service speaks by email alone.

doors.description: A URI template (RFC 6570, level 1) with the one variable address: where the door document of one open-door address is.

carrier.description: One way a step reaches the service directly. This version defines type https (protocol 9.2); a reader ignores any other type.

door.description: An open door's own part of its document: the opaque id a first ask names to reach it, its address, and what it handles.

handle.description: One kind of request an open door takes. Not a promise to answer.

signature.description: One signature: the base64url protected header and the base64url signature. The payload is not carried.
